details:
My partner's club group was suspended for an alleged TOS violation, however to their knowledge (and genuine intent to uphold), nothing in it actually crosses the TOS guidelines.  And if it has... There's nothing in the declaration to say HOW it occurred.  Even the request for a review is a boilerplate "no" and a threat of total account ban if it occurs again, without actually telling them why or how it violated TOS.

So how are they meant to not do so without knowing what actually constituted the TOS violation in the first place?  All you create is a community of groups with a sword of Damocles hanging over every group to fall without knowing why.

Also, while I respect it's gonna mostly be standardized automation when delivering these by necessity, what should be included is at least one or two sentences outlining the actual transgression (eg;  "This line infers such-and-such" or "this part is not permitted by TOS") by the person logging it so that accidental repeat transgressions can't occur.

Additionally, suspending the club owner's account in addition to nuking the group at first offense is way too heavy-handed.  Group privileges mean technically *anyone* in a group can change wording, upload inappropriate photos (not what occurred in this case as photo uploads were not permitted, but broad-strokes possibilities of what can happen in any Group), and there's no real means to definitively say the Owner is always going to be the one at fault.  (Yes, privileges are meant to limit this, but my intent here is that you need to look at the broadest range possible as your baseline range of offenders)

Suspend the group rather than nuke it (unless it's something particularly egregious), warn the Owner of how and why it occurred, and it should end there.  Otherwise you're doing nothing to maintain the communities you're trying to foster on your platform.
title: TOS strikes against Community Groups needs better response, and to not suspend the owner.
